sec(1, "Introduction")
p("This letter sets forth the terms and conditions (the “Agreement”) under which Marcus R. Dunleavy (the “Witness”) will provide information to the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York (the “Office”) in connection with the investigation captioned *United States v. Matsuda of Calder, Finch & Morrow LLP (together, the “Witness’s Counsel”).")
p("The Office and the Witness have agreed that the Witness will participate in a proffer session on **November 14, 2024, at 10:00 a.m.**, at the offices of the United States Attorney, One St. Andrew’s Plaza, New York, New York 10007 (the “Proffer Session”). This Agreement governs the Proffer Session and any continuation of it or any subsequent proffer session that the Office and the Witness’s Counsel agree in writing (including by electronic mail) to conduct pursuant to this Agreement; each such session is included in the term “Proffer Session.” The Witness’s participation is voluntary.")

sec(2, "Definitions")
p("For purposes of this Agreement:")
sub("(a)  “**Proffer Statements**” means (i) all statements, whether oral or written, made by the Witness during the Proffer Session, including factual narratives, responses to questions, identifications, descriptions of documents, and characterizations of events or transactions; (ii) all statements made by the Witness’s Counsel on the Witness’s behalf during the Proffer Session, or in any attorney proffer or other communication with the Office made in connection with arranging or preparing for the Proffer Session, to the extent such statements convey information attributable to the Witness; and (iii) any testimonial or communicative aspect of the Witness’s act of bringing, displaying, or producing the Designated Documents, including any implicit representation as to their existence, possession, custody, control, or authenticity.")
sub("(b)  “**Designated Documents**” means only the approximately six (6) pages of handwritten notes prepared by the Witness of a meeting held on January 12, 2023 at 200 Innovation Drive, White Plains, New York, which the Witness’s Counsel will identify by control numbers [DUNLEAVY-PROFFER-000001 through DUNLEAVY-PROFFER-000006] before the Proffer Session. No other document is a Designated Document unless the Witness’s Counsel so agrees in a writing that identifies the document by control number.")
sub("(c)  “**Proffer Materials**” means, collectively, (i) the Proffer Statements; (ii) the Designated Documents, their contents, and any copy, image, transcription, summary, or description of them; and (iii) all notes, memoranda, reports (including any FBI Form FD-302), summaries, or other records prepared by or for any representative of the Office or any law enforcement agency that memorialize, summarize, or describe any of the foregoing.")
sub("(d)  “**Covered Personnel**” means the Office’s representatives and the agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”) identified in Paragraph 3(a), and any other person employed by the Office or the FBI who is assigned to the Investigation and who receives access to Proffer Materials in accordance with Paragraph 11(b)(i).")

sec(3, "Attendance and Conduct of the Proffer Session")
sub("(a)  **Attendees.** The following persons, and no others, will attend the Proffer Session: for the Office, Assistant United States Attorneys Priya N. Chandrasekaran and Thomas R. Bellamy, FBI Special Agent Darren K. Hollis, and FBI Special Agent Lena M. Torres; and for the Witness, the Witness, Joanna Calder-Reese, and Devon T. Matsuda. No other person may attend any portion of the Proffer Session without the prior written consent of the Witness’s Counsel, which the Office will request at least two (2) business days in advance, identifying the person, his or her agency, and the reason for attendance. No representative of the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”), any other regulatory or law enforcement agency, Helix Biomedical Systems, Inc. (“Helix”), or any other private party will attend or observe any portion of the Proffer Session.")
sub("(b)  **Counsel and consultation.** The Witness’s Counsel may be present throughout the Proffer Session. The Witness may confer privately with the Witness’s Counsel at any time, including before answering any question, and reasonable breaks (including a midday break) will be provided on request.")
sub("(c)  **Right to decline.** The Witness may decline to answer any question or to discuss any subject, including on grounds of privilege, and may end the Proffer Session at any time. Declining to answer a question, declining to produce any document other than the Designated Documents, or ending the Proffer Session shall not constitute a breach of this Agreement and shall not be used against the Witness for any purpose.")
sub("(d)  **Non-adversarial session.** The Proffer Session will be conducted in an informal, non-adversarial manner. No person will be placed under oath.")

sec(4, "Memorialization")
sub("(a)  The Proffer Session will not be audio-recorded, video-recorded, or stenographically transcribed by any person. Covered Personnel may take handwritten or typed notes.")
sub("(b)  Any notes, FBI Form FD-302, or other memorandum of the Proffer Session are Proffer Materials and are subject to every restriction in this Agreement. sub("(c)  Upon the written request of the Witness’s Counsel made within fourteen (14) days after the Proffer Session, the Office will make any FD-302 or other memorandum of the Proffer Session available for review by the Witness’s Counsel at the Office [or, at the Office’s election, will orally review its substance with the Witness’s Counsel]. Within fourteen (14) days after that review, the Witness’s Counsel may submit written corrections or clarifications, which the Office will maintain with the memorandum and will produce together with the memorandum whenever the memorandum is disclosed to any person.")

sec(5, "Use Restrictions — Direct Use")
p("Except as expressly provided in Paragraphs 7 and 8, the Office agrees that it will not offer any Proffer Materials in evidence, or otherwise use them, against the Witness: (a) in its case-in-chief in any criminal prosecution of the Witness; (b) at any sentencing of the Witness, including in determining the applicable range under the United States Sentencing Guidelines, consistent with the principles of U.S.S.G. § 1B1.8; (c) before any grand jury considering whether to return charges against the Witness; or (d) in any civil, administrative, regulatory, or forfeiture proceeding against the Witness. The Office will not argue that the Witness’s willingness to participate in the Proffer Session, or the fact of the Proffer Session, constitutes an admission or evidence of consciousness of guilt.")

sec(6, "Derivative Use")
sub("(a)  **Scope.** The Witness understands that this Agreement is not a grant of immunity under 18 U.S.C. § 6002 and that the protections of *Kastigar v. The Office may pursue investigative leads obtained directly from the Proffer Statements and may use evidence obtained through such leads, subject to the limitations in this Paragraph 6.")
sub("(b)  **Protection of source.** In pursuing any lead, Covered Personnel will not disclose to any person outside the Covered Personnel the fact that the Witness participated in the Proffer Session, that any information originated with the Witness, or the contents of any Proffer Materials, and will not display, read from, or describe the Designated Documents to any witness or other third party.")
sub("(c)  **Record of existing evidence.** Before the Proffer Session begins, the Office will prepare and retain an internal written record, which need not be disclosed to the Witness except in connection with a proceeding described in Paragraph 6(d), identifying the categories of evidence and the principal witnesses then known to the Office concerning the Witness’s conduct.")
sub("(d)  **Burden.** If the Witness challenges any evidence offered against him as having been derived from Proffer Materials, the Office shall bear the burden of establishing, by a preponderance of the evidence, that such evidence was obtained from a legitimate source wholly independent of the Proffer Materials or was in the Office’s possession before the Proffer Session.")

sec(7, "Impeachment and Rebuttal")
sub("(a)  Notwithstanding Paragraph 5, if the Witness testifies as a witness at a federal criminal trial of the Witness arising from the Investigation, and in that testimony makes a statement of fact that is materially inconsistent with a Proffer Statement, the Office may use that Proffer Statement to cross-examine the Witness and to rebut that testimony.")
sub("(b)  [Alternative for negotiation, if required by the Office: The Office may also use a specific Proffer Statement to rebut a factual assertion made by or on behalf of the Witness at such trial, through evidence offered or a factual assertion by counsel, that directly and materially contradicts that specific Proffer Statement. A challenge to the sufficiency of the Office’s evidence, an argument regarding the credibility or weight of the Office’s evidence, or cross-examination that tests the accuracy of a government witness’s testimony without asserting contrary facts shall not trigger this Paragraph 7(b).]")
sub("(c)  This Paragraph 7 does not permit use of (i) any evidence derived from the Proffer Materials, as distinguished from the Proffer Statements themselves; (ii) Proffer Materials in any civil, administrative, regulatory, or other non-criminal proceeding, including *Thornburg v. sub("(d)  Except as expressly provided in this Paragraph 7, the Witness does not waive, and expressly preserves, the protections of Federal Rule of Evidence 410 and Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 11(f). This limited waiver is made knowingly and voluntarily in light of *United States v. Mezzanatto*, 513 U.S. 196 (1995).")

sec(8, "Truthfulness; Correction; Breach")
sub("(a)  **Truthfulness.** The Witness agrees to be truthful in the Proffer Session. The Witness understands that a knowing and willful materially false statement in the Proffer Session may be prosecuted under 18 U.S.C. § 1001, and that such a prosecution is not barred by this Agreement.")
sub("(b)  **Standard.** The Witness breaches this Agreement only if he knowingly and willfully makes a materially false statement of fact, or knowingly and willfully conceals a material fact in an answer he elects to give. None of the following is a breach: a failure or limitation of recollection; an estimate, approximation, or reconstruction identified as such (including as to dollar amounts, dates, or the wording of documents or conversations spanning the period from 2019 through 2024); a statement of opinion, belief, or characterization; a good-faith error; a statement later corrected under Paragraph 8(c); or a decision under Paragraph 3(c) to decline to answer a question or to address a subject.")
sub("(c)  **Correction.** The Witness may, through the Witness’s Counsel, correct, clarify, or supplement any Proffer Statement by written notice to the Office within fourteen (14) business days after the later of (i) the Proffer Session in which the statement was made and (ii) the completion of any review under Paragraph 4(c), or thereafter at any further Proffer Session. A corrected, clarified, or supplemented statement, and the correction itself, remain Proffer Statements and shall not be a basis for a claim of breach.")
sub("(d)  **Notice and determination.** If the Office believes the Witness has breached this Agreement, it will so notify the Witness’s Counsel in writing, identifying each statement it contends is false and the basis for that contention, and will afford the Witness not less than fourteen (14) days to respond. The Office may not treat the Agreement as breached unless, after that period, the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York finds, upon the Office’s application and after notice and an opportunity to be heard, that the Office has established a breach as defined in Paragraph 8(b) by a preponderance of the evidence. Until such a finding, all restrictions in this Agreement remain in full force.")
sub("(e)  **Consequence.** Upon such a finding, the Office will be released from the restrictions in Paragraphs 5, 6, and 7 as to the Proffer Statements made in the Proffer Session in which the breach occurred, and may prosecute the Witness for the false statement. sec(9, "Documents")
sub("(a)  **Designated Documents only.** At the Office’s request, the Witness will bring to the Proffer Session the original Designated Documents. Bringing the Designated Documents is the Witness’s only document-related undertaking under this Agreement.")
sub("(b)  **Inspection.** Covered Personnel may inspect the Designated Documents during the Proffer Session in the presence of the Witness’s Counsel. **[Option A — Inspection Only:]** No copy, photograph, scan, image, or transcription of the Designated Documents will be made or retained by any person other than the Witness’s Counsel, and the originals will remain in the custody of the Witness’s Counsel at all times. **[Option B — Single Controlled Copy:]** The Office may retain one copy of the Designated Documents, bearing their control numbers and the legend “Subject to Proffer Agreement — Dunleavy,” which the Office will maintain in a sealed envelope accessible only to Covered Personnel; no further copies will be made; and, if the Office and the Witness have not entered into a written cooperation or other agreement within ninety (90) days after the Proffer Session, the Office will, upon the written request of the Witness’s Counsel, return or destroy that copy and certify its return or destruction in writing.")
sub("(c)  **Same protection as statements.** The Designated Documents, their contents, and the Witness’s act of bringing or producing them are Proffer Materials and are subject to every restriction in this Agreement to the same extent as oral Proffer Statements. sub("(d)  **No waiver; no representation.** Bringing or producing the Designated Documents does not waive any privilege or protection, including the attorney-client privilege, the protection for attorney work product (including counsel’s mental impressions reflected in the selection of documents), and the Witness’s privilege against self-incrimination, including as to the act of producing any document in response to any subpoena or other process. sub("(e)  **No ongoing obligation.** Nothing in this Agreement, and nothing in the Witness’s bringing or producing the Designated Documents, creates any obligation to produce any other document, record, or tangible item. Any further request by the Office for documents will be made in writing to the Witness’s Counsel. The Witness may decline any such request, and declining shall not be a breach of this Agreement or be used against the Witness. Any further production will occur only pursuant to a separate written agreement or lawful process, and the Witness reserves all objections, privileges, and protections with respect to any such request or process.")

sec(10, "Privileged Matters")
sub("(a)  The Office will not inquire into, and Covered Personnel will not knowingly elicit, (i) communications between the Witness and the Witness’s Counsel or the Witness’s work product; or (ii) communications between the Witness and any attorney for Helix (including Helix’s in-house legal department) or the substance of legal advice provided to Helix. If a question appears to call for such information, the Witness’s Counsel may object, and the Office will withdraw or rephrase the question. The Witness does not purport to waive, and has no authority to waive, any privilege belonging to Helix.")
sub("(b)  Any disclosure of privileged or protected information during the Proffer Session shall be deemed inadvertent and shall not constitute a waiver, by the Witness or by any other holder, of any privilege or protection in this or any other federal or state proceeding, and the Office will not contend otherwise. The parties intend this Paragraph to be applied to the fullest extent permitted under Federal Rule of Evidence 502, including Rules 502(b) and 502(e), and the Office will not oppose an application by the Witness for an order under Rule 502(d) to the same effect.")
sub("(c)  Upon such a disclosure, the Office will not use or disseminate the privileged information, will segregate any notes or memoranda reflecting it, will promptly notify the Witness’s Counsel, and will apply the Office’s filter procedures before any further review by the Investigation team.")

sec(11, "Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure")
sub("(a)  **Undertaking.** The Office and Covered Personnel will hold in confidence, and will not disclose to any person or entity, (i) the fact that the Witness has participated in or agreed to participate in the Proffer Session or has communicated with the Office, (ii) any Proffer Materials, or (iii) information obtained from the Proffer Materials in a form that identifies the Witness as its source. Without limiting the foregoing, this undertaking extends to Helix and its directors, officers, employees, agents, and counsel (including Pemberton Gale LLP); Stanhope & Whitley LLP; Veridian Healthcare Distributors and its personnel and counsel; any target or subject of the Investigation and his or her counsel; the SEC, including staff assigned to *In the Matter of Helix Biomedical Systems, Inc.*, SEC File No. HO-14327; any other federal, state, or local agency, prosecuting office, or self-regulatory organization; any private litigant, including the plaintiffs and counsel in *Thornburg v. Helix Biomedical Systems, Inc., et al.*; and the media.")
sub("(b)  **Exceptions.** Paragraph 11(a) does not apply to disclosure: (i) to employees of the Office and the FBI who are assigned to the Investigation and have a need to know, each of whom will be informed of and bound by this Agreement; (ii) with the prior written consent of the Witness through the Witness’s Counsel; (iii) pursuant to an order of a court of competent jurisdiction entered after the Witness has received notice and an opportunity to be heard; or (iv) required by the Constitution, statute, or rule in a federal criminal case (including the Office’s obligations under *Brady v. Maryland*, *Giglio v. United States*, 18 U.S.C. § 3500, and Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 16), provided that the Office will disclose only what is so required, will give the Witness’s Counsel at least fourteen (14) days’ prior written notice where practicable, and will make the disclosure subject to a protective order restricting its use to the defense of that case and prohibiting its dissemination to Helix, any civil litigant, or any agency.")
sub("(c)  **Parallel proceedings and third-party requests.** The Office will not provide Proffer Materials to the SEC or any other agency through any access request, parallel-proceedings coordination, or informal communication [, and will not share with any such agency information it learns solely from the Proffer Materials]. If the Office receives a subpoena, request under the Freedom of Information Act, or other demand for Proffer Materials, it will promptly notify the Witness’s Counsel and will assert all applicable exemptions and privileges.")
sub("(d)  **Survival.** This Paragraph 11 survives the conclusion or termination of the Proffer Session and any expiration or termination of this Agreement.")

sec(12, "Preservation of Rights")
p("Nothing in this Agreement, and nothing the Witness says or does in the Proffer Session, constitutes a waiver of the Witness’s privilege against self-incrimination under the Fifth Amendment in any proceeding, including *Thornburg v. Helix Biomedical Systems, Inc., et al.* and any SEC investigation or proceeding, and the Office will not contend in any forum that the Witness has waived that privilege by entering into this Agreement or participating in the Proffer Session. The Witness’s decision not to continue the proffer process, not to attend a further session, or not to enter into any further agreement shall not be used against him. Except as expressly stated, this Agreement waives no right, privilege, defense, or objection of the Witness, all of which are reserved.")

sec(13, "No Immunity; No Promises; No Prejudice")
sub("(a)  This Agreement is not an immunity agreement, a non-prosecution agreement, a deferred-prosecution agreement, a cooperation agreement, or a plea agreement. The Office makes no promise regarding the disposition of any potential charges against the Witness, and the decision whether to bring charges remains within the Office’s discretion, subject to the restrictions of this Agreement.")
sub("(b)  Neither the Office nor the Witness is obligated to enter into any further agreement. The Witness’s participation in the Proffer Session, and the Office’s assessment of it, shall not prejudice the ability of the Witness and the Office to negotiate any future agreement, and the terms of this Agreement shall not serve as a minimum or maximum for, or otherwise limit, the terms of any such agreement.")

sec(14, "Parties Bound")
p("This Agreement binds the Office and the Witness. The Office will ensure that all Covered Personnel comply with this Agreement. This Agreement does not bind any other United States Attorney’s Office, component of the Department of Justice, or agency, except that the Office’s undertakings in Paragraphs 6(b), 9, 10, and 11 govern the Office’s own conduct with respect to every such office and agency.")

sec(15, "Termination of a Session; Modification")
p("Either the Office or the Witness may end the Proffer Session at any time. The restrictions of this Agreement remain in full force as to all Proffer Materials generated before the end of the Proffer Session, regardless of which party ends it or why, subject only to Paragraph 8. This Agreement may be modified only by a writing signed by the Office, the Witness, and the Witness’s Counsel, except that the scheduling of a subsequent session under Paragraph 1 may be confirmed by electronic mail between the Office and the Witness’s Counsel.")

sec(16, "Entire Agreement; Interpretation; Counterparts")
p("This letter is the entire agreement among the Office, the Witness, and the Witness’s Counsel concerning the Proffer Session and supersedes all prior communications concerning its terms, including the Office’s electronic mail of October 21, 2024, to the extent inconsistent with this Agreement. No promises, agreements, or conditions have been made other than those set forth in this letter. This Agreement shall be interpreted in accordance with the principles of contract law that govern agreements between the government and individuals in criminal matters in this Circuit. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which shall be deemed an original.")

h("I. Purpose and Bottom Line")
p("Attached for your review is a defense draft of the proffer agreement for Mr. Dunleavy’s November 14, 2024 session (file: *proffer-agreement-draft.docx*). It is built on the firm’s SDNY template (WC-PRO-003, March 2023), conformed to the facts and to AUSA Chandrasekaran’s October 21, 2024 email, and rewritten to carry each recommendation in my October 25 case memorandum. Because I did not receive direction on the open questions by October 28, the draft takes the defense-favorable position on each and puts the main alternatives in brackets so you can choose before we transmit.")
p("**Bottom line.** The draft is an opening position, not where we expect to end up. The email describes three terms as standard and says one of them (impeachment and rebuttal) is “non-negotiable,” and it says the Office “does not anticipate agreeing to material changes.” We should expect to give ground on derivative use, the judicial-determination mechanism for breach, and the forum limits on impeachment. We should hold firm on: (1) document treatment and the “no ongoing obligation” clause; (2) the confidentiality and non-disclosure protections (Helix, the SEC, and private litigants); (3) a knowing-and-willful truthfulness standard with a right to correct; and (4) no waiver of the Fifth Amendment or of privilege. Section V gives the priorities and fallbacks.")
p("**Before transmittal:** (i) choose among the bracketed alternatives (¶¶ 4(c), 7(b), 9(b), 11(c)); (ii) remove the “Defense Proposed Draft” header if you prefer to send a clean draft with a cover email; (iii) fill in the control numbers for the January 12, 2023 notes once we Bates-stamp them; and (iv) cite-check the authorities cited here (see Section VIII).")

h("IV. Issues Found in File Review Not Fully Captured in the October 25 Memorandum")
heading(d, "A. The government’s email is broader than the October 25 memo’s summary of it", underline=False, before=4)
p("Section IV of my October 25 memorandum summarized the call, but the October 21 email goes further in several places. The draft responds to the email as written:")
b("**Impeachment trigger.** The email lets the Office use proffer statements, and *documents produced*, wherever Dunleavy “or his counsel offers testimony or makes representations” that are inconsistent. This is a counsel-triggered rebuttal waiver of the kind the Second Circuit has enforced, under which factual assertions made through counsel (for example, in an opening statement or on cross-examination) can open the door (see *United States v. Velez*, 354 F.3d 190 (2d Cir. 2004); *United States v. Barrow*, 400 F.3d 109 (2d Cir. 2005); *cf. United States v. Rosemond*, 841 F.3d 95 (2d Cir. 2016)). It is a real constraint on any trial defense, which is why ¶7(b) is drafted as a narrow fallback rather than left open.")
b("**Derivative use.** The email allows leads “derived directly or indirectly” and use of the resulting evidence “without limitation.” The October 25 memo’s third derivative-use point (do not exceed what the AUSA articulated) therefore gives us little protection. The template and the email already go to the outer limit.")
b("**Truthfulness.** The email adds “materially incomplete” and says the duty “extends to all topics … without limitation” and that he “must be prepared to answer all questions fully.” Read literally, a refusal to answer on privilege grounds could be called a breach. Draft ¶¶3(c) and 8(b) address this directly.")
b("**Additional attendees and documents.** The email reserves the right to bring additional law enforcement personnel and to ask for “additional documents or records in his possession.” This confirms the gateway concern. Draft ¶¶3(a) and 9(e) close both doors.")
b("**Copying.** The email asks to “review and copy” the notes. Option A (inspection only) directly rejects that request. Expect pushback, which is why Option B is there.")

heading(d, "B. Equity plan: confidentiality is necessary but will not by itself protect the $1.2 million in options", underline=False, before=6)
p("The October 25 memo treats forfeiture mainly as a risk that Helix learns of the cooperation. Section 7.4 of the plan is broader than that:")
b("**§ 7.4(c)(C) may already be triggered.** Unvested awards are subject to forfeiture if the participant is a named defendant in a shareholder action. Dunleavy has been a named defendant in *Thornburg* since August 15, 2024. Under § 7.4(c), being “involved in” a criminal investigation in which he is a “target, subject, or defendant” is also a trigger (§ 7.4(c)(A)), as is being named a target or subject by “any governmental authority … or the Company.” The forfeiture risk therefore exists today, independent of the proffer.")
b("**§ 7.4(e)(iii) makes voluntary assistance itself “Conduct Detrimental.”** It bars “voluntarily providing information, documents, testimony, or other assistance” in a proceeding adverse to the Company or its officers, “unless compelled to do so by lawful process.” A voluntary proffer and voluntary production of the notes fall squarely within that language. Under § 7.4(b) this exposes both vested and unvested awards to forfeiture and permits a 36-month clawback of gains, at any time through 24 months after termination (that is, through about September 6, 2026). The Committee needs no notice or hearing (§ 7.4(b)), and its decisions are “final and binding” (§ 7.4(d)).")
b("**The lawful-process exception creates a trade-off to decide (open question 6(b)).** Producing the notes under a grand jury subpoena would bring the production within the plan’s “compelled … by lawful process” exception. But it would forfeit the inspection-only approach, and a subpoena response is not a Proffer Material. Under *Fisher v. United States*, 425 U.S. 391 (1976), the contents of voluntarily prepared papers are not privileged. The act of production may be (*United States v. Doe*, 465 U.S. 605 (1984); *United States v. Hubbell*, 530 U.S. 27 (2000)). Draft ¶¶2(a)(iii), 9(c) and 9(d) therefore treat the voluntary act of production as a protected Proffer Statement and preserve the act-of-production privilege for any later subpoena. I recommend we stay with voluntary inspection under the agreement and handle the plan risk through confidentiality and employment counsel, not through a subpoena. This is your call.")
b("**Possible limits on the plan’s enforceability.** Section 7.4(e)(iii), as applied to assistance to federal law enforcement or the SEC, may be limited by the whistleblower protections of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (18 U.S.C. § 1514A) and by SEC Rule 21F-17(a), which prohibits impeding communications with SEC staff. Separately, the September 6, 2024 termination followed documented internal objections (November 3, 2021; February 14, 2023). That could support a SOX retaliation claim, which must be filed with OSHA within 180 days (on my count, by about March 5, 2025). Dunleavy’s own participation complicates both theories, and I have not researched either one. I recommend referring them to employment counsel now. We should also obtain his termination letter and award agreements, because the October 25 memo notes that the “for cause” designation is unclear. If the termination was for Cause, § 7.4(a) required any vested options to be exercised within 10 days (by about September 16, 2024).")

heading(d, "C. The in-house counsel privilege belongs to Helix, not to Dunleavy", underline=False, before=6)
p("The October 25 memo frames the privilege issue as Dunleavy’s own potential waiver. His declaration (¶22) describes his dealings with Helix’s in-house legal department as potentially subject to *Helix’s* privilege. That privilege belongs to the corporation, and Dunleavy cannot waive it. The real risks are different: (i) disclosure would hand Helix and Pemberton Gale a grievance, and possibly “Conduct Detrimental” grounds under § 7.4(f)(ii)(C); and (ii) privileged material could taint the government’s team. Draft ¶10 therefore (a) prohibits eliciting Helix legal advice, (b) says expressly that he does not purport to waive Helix’s privilege, and (c) requires filter procedures. Rule 502 governs disclosures “to a federal office or agency.” Its application to oral proffer statements is unsettled, which is why ¶10(b) also invites a Rule 502(d) order. Preparation must cover this point (Section VI).")

heading(d, "D. Mandatory disclosure will eventually reach the co-defendants", underline=False, before=6)
p("If Moorfield, Dunmore, Haynes or Kirkwood is charged, the Office’s Brady, Giglio, § 3500 and Rule 16 obligations may require it to produce proffer material relating to Dunleavy. Information that reaches Dunmore or Moorfield may reach Helix. The Office will not accept an absolute bar, and an absolute bar would be unenforceable against constitutional obligations. Draft ¶11(b)(iv) instead requires minimum necessary disclosure, 14 days’ notice where practicable, and a protective order that bars dissemination to Helix, civil litigants and agencies. This is a realistic and defensible ask. It also makes the confidentiality clause more credible, because it does not ask the Office to promise the impossible.")

heading(d, "E. Dunleavy’s status is unconfirmed", underline=False, before=6)
p("The file lists Moorfield and Dunmore as targets and Haynes and Kirkwood as subjects, but nothing records Dunleavy’s status, and the declaration (¶41) says he has received no subpoena. Before the session we should ask AUSA Chandrasekaran to confirm whether he is a target or a subject (see Justice Manual § 9-11.151). The answer affects our risk assessment and may itself trigger § 7.4(c) of the plan. We should therefore ask orally and not memorialize it in the agreement.")

heading(d, "F. The client declaration and recollection limits", underline=False, before=6)
p("Dunleavy’s draft declaration says his quarterly figures and the wording of conversations are reconstructions (¶¶16, 43). It also gives only annual totals. The quarter-by-quarter breakdown appears only in our October 25 memo. That supports the safe harbor for estimates and the correction right in ¶8. It also means that in preparation he should not adopt figures more precise than he can personally support. Two further cautions: (i) the declaration contains detailed admissions and is framed “under penalty of perjury,” so I recommend it remain an unsigned, privileged working document and not be executed or produced; and (ii) as you directed, nothing in the agreement refers to the Graystone polygraph of October 8, 2024.")

h("V. Recommended Negotiating Priorities")
b("**Tier 1 (hold firm):** documents get the same protection as statements, and there is no ongoing production obligation (¶9(c)–(e)); confidentiality as to the fact of the proffer and as to Helix, the SEC and private litigants (¶11(a)–(c)); a knowing-and-willful truthfulness standard with a correction right (¶8(b)–(c)); no Fifth Amendment or privilege waiver (¶¶10, 12); no impeachment use in non-criminal forums, including Thornburg and the SEC (¶7(c)(ii)).")
b("**Tier 2 (push, with fallbacks):** written notice of breach plus a judicial determination (fallback: notice and an opportunity to respond); 302 review (fallback: oral read-back plus a corrections letter); a closed attendee list (fallback: notice plus a right to object); inspection only (fallback: Option B).")
b("**Tier 3 (likely to concede):** limiting derivative use to direct leads and shifting the burden to the Office (keep source protection and the pre-session evidence record if possible); no grand jury or sentencing use; the bracketed ¶11(c) “derived information” clause; limiting impeachment to his own testimony (concede ¶7(b) if needed).")

h("VI. Responses to the Open Questions in the October 25 Memorandum (Item 6)")
b("**(a) Derivative use:** treat our position as an opening position. The email shows the Office will not move on the core point. I would spend our negotiating capital on Tier 1 and keep the source-protection and pre-session record provisions as the realistic ask.")
b("**(b) The notes:** bring them for inspection only (Option A), with Option B as the fallback. Do not hand over copies outside the agreement. If you prefer the plan’s lawful-process exception (Section IV.B), we would need to restructure ¶9 around a narrow subpoena.")
b("**(c) SEC non-disclosure:** treat it as a deal-breaker only as to the *fact* of the proffer and the Proffer Materials themselves. Treat the “derived information” clause as a strong preference. Given the confirmed USAO–SEC contact and the plan’s regulatory-proceeding trigger (§ 7.4(c)(B)), the core bar is worth the friction.")
b("**(d) Reference to future cooperation:** the draft does not name a cooperation agreement. ¶13(b) preserves our ability to negotiate one (“neither a minimum nor a maximum”) without signaling expectations. I recommend leaving it that way.")
b("**(e) Thornburg stay:** coordinate the timing with the session. I would aim to move after November 14, once we know whether a cooperation track is opening. ¶¶7(c)(ii) and 12 are drafted so that his Fifth Amendment posture in Thornburg is unaffected either way.")

h("VII. Next Steps")
